chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from some of our companions from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as 'a mercy to the worlds' on the 27th of Rajab; so whoever fasts that day, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, records for him the fasting of sixty months.

And on the 25th of Dhi al-Qa'dah, Allah established the House (Kaaba), which is the first mercy established upon the face of the earth; so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made it 'a place of return for the people and a sanctuary'; so whoever fasts that day, Allah records for him the fasting of sixty months.
And on the first day of Dhi al-Hijjah, Ibrahim (Abraham), the friend of the Merciful, was born; so whoever fasts that day, Allah records for him the fasting of sixty months.

key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: The House (referring to the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.خَلِيلُ الرَّحْمَنِ: The friend of the Merciful (epithet for Ibrahim)
key_terms.ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhi al-Qa'dah (the 11th month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.رَحْمَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ: A mercy to the worlds (Quranic epithet for the Prophet)
key_terms.مَثَابَةً لِلنَّاسِ: A place of return for the people (Quranic description of the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues of fasting on the 27th of Rajab and the 1st of Dhi al-Hijjah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the spiritual merit of fasting on three pivotal dates: the 27th of Rajab (Prophet's mission), the 25th of Dhi al-Qa'dah (Kaaba's establishment), and the 1st of Dhi al-Hijjah (Ibrahim's birth). Each fast yields the reward of sixty months, reflecting the concept of *thawab al-mu'addal* (multiplied reward) for commemorating foundational events in Islamic history. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on linking devotional acts to the historical milestones of the Prophets and the sanctity of the Kaaba.
